#### 1. red-green color blindness  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.488)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2187335)

**Proposed mechanism:** RBP3 pathogenic variant (null) —DISRUPTS→ RBP3 (HGNC:9947); RBP3 (HGNC:9947) —DECREASES→ Photoreceptor function and development (GO:0000344); Photoreceptor function and development (GO:0000344) —LEADS_TO→ Retinitis Pigmentosa 72 (MONDO:0014093); OPN1MW pathogenic variant (null) —DISRUPTS→ OPN1MW (HGNC:8707); OPN1MW (HGNC:8707) —DECREASES→ Photoreceptor function and development (GO:0000344); Photoreceptor function and development (GO:0000344) —LEADS_TO→ Red-green color blindness (MONDO:0010564). Pathogenic variants in RBP3 lead to Retinitis Pigmentosa 72 through disruption of RBP3 and subsequent impairment of photoreceptor function and development. Similarly, pathogenic variants in OPN1MW lead to red-green color blindness by disrupting OPN1MW and impairing the same general pathway of photoreceptor function and development. The convergence is on the shared biological pathway critical for visual processing.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in RBP3 or OPN1MW in individuals with the other disease's phenotype, without any other identifiable genetic cause for their condition, would support this link. Conversely, if individuals with Retinitis Pigmentosa 72 are found to have completely normal OPN1MW function and individuals with red-green color blindness have normal RBP3 function, this would weaken the proposed overlap. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD in the coding regions of RBP3 and OPN1MW that are associated with severe loss-of-function phenotypes would suggest that these genes are generally tolerant to variation and may not be the sole drivers of these specific rare disease phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of photoreceptor function and development could reveal novel therapeutic targets applicable to both retinitis pigmentosa and color blindness. For example, gene therapy approaches aimed at restoring function within this pathway might offer benefits across both disease spectra.
